svg.title: One analysis, replayed, then escalated
svg.desc: A looping picture in two laps of about 13 seconds each, 26 seconds in all. A chip row at the top says which lap is playing. Lap 1 is a recording of one analysis, from a Warning event to a verified pull request: release v0.3.0-rc.2, an OOMKilled workload, 3 min 34 s from symptom to pull request. An OOMKilled event becomes an Incident. The analyzer builds the context and redacts it: a secret value in the input is replaced by the placeholder [REDACTED:credential]. The triage model answers with one call, and the answer becomes a typed proposal. The escalation path is always drawn: from the triage model a branch leads to an escalation model, with the read tools offered to it (get_resource, list_events, get_pod_logs, query_metrics, check_missing_reference), and from there back to the proposal. It is taken when the context builder cut the context or could not fetch a source, or when the triage reply failed schema validation after one retry. In the recorded run it was not taken, so lap 1 draws it dim and says so. Lap 2 is an illustration, not a recording, and carries no numbers: the same flow, with the dot going through the escalation model. The read tools are drawn as offered to the model by a dashed line; the picture does not show a tool call. The executor checks the proposal against the fixed list of changes and the policy, then opens a pull request in the GitOps repository. A person reviews and merges it, Flux applies the commit, and the verifier reads the pods and ends the request. Shown in red: nothing, neither the analyzer, the model nor the executor, has a path to the workloads; only Flux changes them. With reduced motion set, the picture is still and shows both paths, both lap labels and both captions at once.

g.text: changed only by Flux, after a person merges

svg.text: Lap 1, recorded run, not live: v0.3.0-rc.2, an OOMKilled workload. 3 min 34 s from symptom to pull request, shown here in 13 s. The escalation path was not taken.
Lap 2, illustration, not a recording and without numbers: the same flow through the escalation model. The read tools are offered to it; no call is shown.
